name: Rome, Italy 🇮🇹
subtitle: Cacio e pepe, supplì, and carbonara — the eternal table
items: Roscioli (Campo de' Fiori, deli + restaurant — best cacio e pepe in Rome, period. Book weeks ahead)
Pizzarium (Prati, Gabriele Bonci — pizza al taglio, sold by weight, international pilgrimage)
Flavio al Velavevodetto (Testaccio, Flavio De Maio — rigatoni alla pajata in the quarter that invented offal)
Da Remo (Testaccio, cash-only pizza, neighborhood legend)
Checchino dal 1887 (Testaccio, since 1887 — the quinto quarto specialists, historic Roman)
La Pergola (Monte Mario, Heinz Beck, 3-star — the only 3-star in Rome, views of the city)
Il Pagliaccio (Campo de' Fiori area, Anthony Genovese, 2-star)
Armando al Pantheon (Pantheon, Armando Gargioli — Roman classics, since 1961, book ahead)
Osteria dell'Orso (Tiber, medieval palazzo — traditional Roman)
Supplì Roma (Trastevere + Testaccio, the benchmark suppli al telefono)
Tonnarello (Trastevere, classic trattoria, outdoor terrace)
Grazia & Graziella (Garbatella — Romans only, traditional Roman, off the tourist map)
Pizzeria da Baffetto (Via del Governo Vecchio, thin-crust Roman pizza, cash only, queue)
Ristorante Il Sorpasso (Prati, modern Roman wine bar)
Antico Arco (Gianicolo, fine dining, views, Alessandro Pierini)
Mercato di Campo de' Fiori (morning market — produce, flowers, daily life)
Mercato Testaccio (the new Testaccio market hall — the food hall Rome deserves)
Gelateria dei Gracchi (Prati, best gelato in Rome — pistachio, hazelnut)
Bar San Calisto (Trastevere — the most Roman bar experience, very cheap)
Café Sant'Eustachio (Pantheon, the best espresso in Rome, non-negotiable)
